name: Exploitation for Client Execution
description:
Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in client applications to execute code. Vulnerabilities can exist in software due to insecure coding practices that can lead to unanticipated behavior. Adversaries may take advantage of certain vulnerabilities through targeted exploitation for the purpose of arbitrary code execution. Oftentimes the most valuable exploits to an offensive toolkit are those that can be used to obtain code execution on a remote system because they can be used to gain access to that system. Users will expect to see files related to the applications they commonly used to do work, so they are a useful target for exploit research and development because of their high utility. 

Adversaries may use device-based zero-click exploits for code execution. These exploits are powerful because there is no user interaction required for code execution. 

### SMS/iMessage Delivery  

SMS and iMessage in iOS are common targets through [Drive-By Compromise](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1456), [Phishing](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1660), etc. Adversaries may use embed malicious links, files, etc. in SMS messages or iMessages. Mobile devices may be compromised through one-click exploits, where the victim must interact with a text message, or zero-click exploits, where no user interaction is required. 

### AirDrop 

Unique to iOS, AirDrop is a network protocol that allows iOS users to transfer files between iOS devices. Before patches from Apple were released, on iOS 13.4 and earlier, adversaries may force the Apple Wireless Direct Link (AWDL) interface to activate, then exploit a buffer overflow to gain access to the device and run as root without interaction from the user.

telemetry.name: Host Status
telemetry.description: Host health and availability observations such as heartbeat, shutdown or degraded state.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect agent heartbeat and OS health independently; record missed polls, last-seen time and monitor health.

providers.name: osquery
providers.scope: Scheduled host-state queries; supported tables and privileges vary by OS. Select a table that actually exposes the required object.

providers.name: Linux Audit plus inventory snapshots
providers.scope: Events explain changes; snapshots describe state at collection time.

configuration: Define the inventory query, allowed host set, interval and least-privileged reader. Store a stable asset ID, observation time and collector version.
Keep successive snapshots and calculate additions, removals and changed attributes. Pair state changes with audit events when available.
Export collector health and missed-poll counts so a missing snapshot is not misclassified as a missing asset.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Snapshots miss short-lived objects and do not identify who caused a change. A generic inventory agent is not guaranteed to expose firmware or kernel-level details.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Compare authorized state snapshots: first-seen drivers/services/modules, unexpected configuration drift and integrity changes. Record collection cadence; absence in a sample is not evidence of deletion.

telemetry.name: Network Connection Creation
telemetry.description: Creation of an endpoint network connection linked to a process.
telemetry.collection_focus: Enable scoped Sysmon NetworkConnect (3), disabled by default, or a platform-equivalent process-aware network sensor.

providers.name: Microsoft Sysmon
providers.scope: Windows event-based collection; enable the event types needed below.

providers.name: Linux Audit
providers.scope: Linux alternative for supported system-call and file events; different semantics and fields.

providers.name: Apple Endpoint Security clients
providers.scope: macOS alternative where the subscribed event exists; requires an entitled, approved client, not an iOS collector.

configuration: On a disposable Windows host, review the installed Sysmon schema and current configuration; merge scoped event filters into the existing policy rather than replacing it.
Forward Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational to the lab collector. Preserve event ID, timestamp, computer, process identifiers and the original event.
For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Event filtering and sensor versions change coverage. High-volume image-load and process-access collection needs tuning; endpoint events alone do not establish intent.

strategies.name: Detection of Exploitation for Client Execution

analytics.name: Analytic 1699
analytics.guidance: For Android, detect Exploitation for Client Execution by correlating analyst-visible device/network evidence and management state; use streaming or batched telemetry only where the documented collector is deployed. Correlate Host Status via Android Enterprise DPC [DevicePolicyManager policy/compliance/security-state queries and SecurityLog events where supported]; Network Connection Creation via Android Enterprise Network Logging / Enterprise VPN [DevicePolicyManager.retrieveNetworkLogs(): DnsEvent / ConnectEvent; VPN flow metadata]; Process Creation via Application Vetting / Managed Device Telemetry [execve()]. Alert on a sequence or state change inconsistent with the device/app baseline, approved management policy, or expected user workflow; do not infer unobserved API calls, file/process activity, or payload content from management state alone.

tuning.description: mediaserver, chromium, com.android.browser, com.android.mms, com.android.messaging. Expand per installed browser.
Renderer, GPU process, sandboxed service workers. Derive from media process baseline.
Default 10s between media process activity and child spawn.
Default 30s between child spawn and C2 connection.
Default 30 days. Context only — not primary signal.

log_sources.channel: DevicePolicyManager policy/compliance/security-state queries and SecurityLog events where supported

analytics.name: Analytic 1700
analytics.guidance: For iOS, detect Exploitation for Client Execution by correlating analyst-visible device/network evidence and management state; use streaming or batched telemetry only where the documented collector is deployed. Correlate Host Status via Apple MDM [DeviceInformation / SecurityInfo / ProfileList / restrictions and compliance queries]; Network Connection Creation via Apple Network Extension / Enterprise VPN [NEFilterFlow / per-app VPN / secure-web-gateway flow metadata]; Process Creation via Application Vetting / Managed Device Telemetry [com.apple.WebContent or com.apple.imagent process shows unexpected child spawn or memory fault at level=fault in Unified Log — kernel fault in message-processing subsystem is exploit execution signal]. Alert on a sequence or state change inconsistent with the device/app baseline, approved management policy, or expected user workflow; do not infer unobserved API calls, file/process activity, or payload content from management state alone.

tuning.description: Known Apple CDN, update, and push notification server IP ranges. Derive from Apple published IP lists.

software.name: Pegasus for iOS
software.description: [Pegasus for iOS](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0289) can compromise iPhones running iOS 16.6 without any user interaction.(Citation: Scott-Railton_TheCitizenLab Pegasus Apr2022)

references.description: Scott-Railton, J., et al. (2022, April 18). Extensive Mercenary Spyware Operation against Catalans Using Pegasus and Candiru. Retrieved April 18, 2024.

software.name: LightSpy
software.description: [LightSpy](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1185) has compromised iPhones running iOS 12.1 and 12.2 without any user interaction.(Citation: Shoshin_Kaspersky LightSpy 2020)

references.description: Shoshin, P. (2020, March 27). LightSpy spyware targets iPhone users in Hong Kong. Retrieved February 12, 2025.

mitigations.name: Security Updates
mitigations.description: Security updates frequently contain patches to vulnerabilities.

mitigations.name: User Guidance
mitigations.description: Users should be wary of iMessages from unknown senders. Additionally, users should be instructed not to open unrecognized links or other attachments in text messages.

simulation.prerequisites: Use owned test devices or emulators, disposable app accounts and test data. Verify platform/version instrumentation; desktop test procedures do not establish mobile coverage.

synthetic.purpose: Collection/parser contract exercise, NOT a positive example or detection of this TTP.
